credentials.description: API key of the environment (sandbox and production keys differ, from the Dashboard)
partner ID — numeric, no leading zeros (Dashboard)

parameters.name: job_id
parameters.description: TypeID format verification identifier with 'job_' prefix. Passed as a path parameter.

example_prompt: Ask Smile ID to re-send the result webhook of a completed verification, e.g. after all delivery attempts to your callback_url failed.

callback_url.description: Override callback URL. Must be on the partner's callback domain allowlist. If omitted, the stored callback URL is used. Can also be provided via the token payload (see /v3/token).

input_schema.description: job_id goes in the path; the optional multipart/form-data body only carries callback_url.

status.description: Always 'accepted' for successful replay requests. 'accepted' in the OpenAPI; 'Accepted' in the migration guide and the Web SDK page.

user_id.description: User ID associated with the verification (from partner_params).

gotchas: Auth: mint a token with POST /v3/token, then send SmileID-Partner-ID and SmileID-Token on this request (auth.token_exchange / auth.apply). Docs (Authentication): "Access tokens expire **15 minutes** after issuance. We recommend generating a new token for every verification request rather than reusing tokens across multiple requests." Mint tokens on your backend only: the API key never goes to the browser. The endpoint's OpenAPI declares only SmileID-Token; the Authentication page requires both headers — send both.

This is the way to get the full verification result again: Smile ID retries a failed webhook 3 times (4 attempts in total), then stops. The replay is queued (202) and the payload arrives on the callback URL, not in this response.
The job must be in a terminal state (clear, block, attention, error) — otherwise 409. Poll get_verification_status first.
An optional callback_url overrides the stored one but must be on the partner's callback domain allowlist (403 otherwise). If a body is sent it must be multipart/form-data (415).
The 202 body's status is 'accepted' in the OpenAPI; other pages spell the acceptance status 'Accepted' — compare case-insensitively.
Keys, tokens and callback URLs are environment-specific: a sandbox token returns 401 in production.

spans: The verification must have reached a terminal state (clear, block, attention, or error) before its callback can be replayed.
